title: Long-term care facility emergency medication kit under 105 CMR 150.008(E)
rule_summary: Under 105 CMR 150.008(E) an emergency medication kit shall be provided in all long-term care facilities. (1) The contents of the kit shall be approved by the Department; in a SNCFC a pediatric emergency kit and emergency resuscitation equipment and medication shall be provided, with a chart listing pediatric doses for emergency drugs included with the emergency equipment. (2) The kit shall be kept in a separate, sealed container stored in a suitable place when not in use, and drugs requiring refrigeration shall be kept in a separate sealed container under proper refrigeration. (3) Each kit shall be prepared, packaged and sealed by a pharmacist and shall contain a list of contents on the outside cover and within the box. (4) The medications in the kit shall be used only upon the orders of a primary care provider. (5) After a kit has been opened, it shall be inspected, re-stocked and resealed by the pharmacist within 48 hours prior to further use.
exam_relevance: Tests the Department's facility-side rules for the kit, including the pharmacist's preparation and sealing, the contents list in two places, use only on a primary care provider's order, and the 48-hour re-sealing after opening.

authority.name: 105 CMR 150.000: Standards for Long-Term Care Facilities

numeric_facts.fact: period for the pharmacist to inspect, re-stock and reseal an opened kit
numeric_facts.conditions: after the kit has been opened, prior to further use; 105 CMR 150.008(E)(5)

common_confusions: The kit is prepared, packaged and sealed by a pharmacist, and after opening it is inspected, re-stocked and resealed by the pharmacist, not by facility nursing staff.
Kit contents are approved by the Department; the controlled-substance list in the Department's circular letter was developed under 150.008(E)(1).
